  set of second items in each coll, until any one of the colls is
  exhausted.  Any remaining items in other colls are ignored. Function
  f should accept number-of-colls arguments. Returns a transducer when

rationale: Preserve the complete pinned declaration, documentation, every arity and every branch. Expand defn to def/fn, lazy-seq to the pinned owned LazySeq constructor with fn*, when-let to a once-only temporary and conditional inner binding, and dotimes to its exact bounded let/loop/when algorithm with qualified comparison/inc calls. Keep transducer initialization/completion/variadic reducer arities, multi-input shortest-sequence behavior, named step recursion, ordered chunk filling and repeated nth reads. Existing portable owned-array macro/nominal adapters are dependencies, not full make-array extraction evidence. Native execution, pinned value/effect observations and final acceptance are required; this adaptation remains in progress. Expand the single pinned shorthand #(apply f %) to an explicit one-parameter fn* preserving its captured f and live apply; this is not general reader support. Canonical ArrayChunk indexed reads try a guarded callback-free Object[] helper, retaining the original -nth call for other receivers/storage/indices. The local chunk count is a raw long, widening the JVM ICounted int result once before the loop without adding a primitive function-call boundary. Source callback order and generic fallbacks are retained. Use an owned Object[] output buffer directly: it is private to the thunk and never exposed to callbacks, so the per-item ChunkBuffer count and method dispatch are unobservable. Map writes the corresponding index; filter tracks its compacted output index, retaining the value captured before the predicate. Construct the published ArrayChunk only after the ordered callbacks/stores complete. A canonical well-formed Object[] input chunk admits a loop-invariant typed array view and immutable offset, with each element read in its original callback order; unsupported chunks retain one -nth call per item. Only storage/immutable metadata are hoisted, never element values. Numeric local metadata alone does not insert a physical conversion. Use explicit inline long casts for the ICounted result and admitted immutable offset, and for str loop state read back from its temporary pair, so the IR carries raw longs through arithmetic/array indexing without adding a primitive function entry. Early core definitions precede the public long var; the private long-cast word emits the same existing checked LongCast operation. The private long-add compiler word uses the existing checked non-coercing raw arithmetic for bounded long offsets/counters and geometric output growth; legacy coercing core arithmetic would otherwise box these operations. Values are evaluated in order and overflow still follows the existing checked arithmetic route. All chunk/native storage words require trusted compilation, including when ordinary source selects the suss.core namespace.
